03 / FIELD NOTES

Before you feed the plotter.

Paper, pens, and things worth checking.

01 Find a starting point +

Open a drawer above and compare its specimens. Choose Make this drawing to load that specimen’s saved controls. Change one thing at a time to see what it does.

02 Understand the marks +

Hatching makes tone from parallel strokes. Seeds make chance repeatable. In hidden-message studios, the drawing carries information: keep the reading key and machine marks when you want to decode it later.

03 Put it on paper +

Export a millimetre SVG from the studio. In Design Space, set the artwork to Pen, check its physical size, Attach, then Make. For separate pen files, keep the paper on the mat and align the same corner ticks between passes.

04 Read it back +

For supported hidden-message plots, use the camera decoder with the required marks and settings. A clean gallery copy and a machine-readable plot can need different exports.

Open the plot decoder ↗
01 Start with a silhouette +

Open a lino drawer and choose Make this cut to load its saved controls. Change the subject, frame, gouges or size in the studio.

02 Keep and weed +

Filled shapes are the vinyl you keep. Holes and the surrounding material are weeded away. The studio checks closed loops, narrow strips, small pieces and gaps before export.

03 Send it to the blade +

Export the decal cut layer from the studio. In Design Space, set it to Basic Cut, check the millimetre size and keep any weeding box aligned. Choose the material settings for your vinyl and make a small test cut first; physical cut sizes are untested.

04 Transfer the result +

For adhesive vinyl, weed the waste and use transfer tape to place the decal. For iron-on, the studio already mirrors the export: do not mirror it again in Design Space.
